newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldier shoots, wounds Arabs in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier shoots, wounds Arabs in Hebron.

text.p: An Israeli soldier opened fire in all directions in the West Bank town of Hebron, wounding at least three Palestinians in the Arab market on Wednesday, witnesses said.
It was not immediately clear why the gunman opened fire. Witnesses said soldiers arrested the man and seized his gun.
They said at least three Palestinians were wounded.
The incident occurred just as Israel and the Palestinians neared a deal for Israel to hand over most of the West Bank town to Palestinian self-rule.

Witnesses said he was a young man who wore an army uniform and on his head the skullcap of a religious Jew. It was not immediately clear if he was on duty in the town, a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence.
Israeli Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told army radio he did not expect the incident to affect plans by Israel and the PLO to press ahead with a deal on Hebron.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said earlier on Wednesday he and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had yet to fix a summit to sew up a deal giving self-rule to Hebron.
Some 400 Jews live in the heart of the town, a flashpoint of violence and home to 100,000 Arabs.

Three years ago a Jew from nearby Kiryat Arba settlement, dressed in an Israeli army uniform, massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers in the tomb of the biblical patriarchs before survivors beat him to death.

The sides greeted the new year much the way they had spent the old one -- haggling over promised withdrawals and elusive peace deals. The handover of most of Hebron to the Palestinians has been delayed for nine months by Israeli security concerns.

Jewish settlers in the town had said they were praying for a miracle to prevent Israeli troops from pulling back and warned of impending bloodshed. They scuffled with Palestinians on Tuesday and tried to take over Arab houses in the casbah.
"I appeal even at this moment to the prime minister: Don't sign an agreement that will endanger our lives," Hebron settler leader Rabbi Moshe Levinger told Israel Radio on Wednesday.
Jewish settlers, who number 130,000 in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, helped Netanyahu sweep to power in elections last May on a promise to be tough with the Palestinians.
But Netanyahu has come under pressure from Washington, Israel's closest ally, to honour peace deals and withdraw from Hebron, the last of seven West Bank towns due for self-rule.
